validity.value: No more than 3 months old — consistently confirmed by both the Consulate General of Grenada (Miami) and the High Commission for Grenada (UK): "TWO (2) Passport pictures (no more than 3 months old), one certified by a Justice of the Peace or a Notary Public."

cross_verification.note_en: Two official Grenada missions were read directly (PDF text via the Read tool): Consulate General of Grenada, Miami and High Commission for Grenada, UK. Both give an identical procedural requirement — 'no more than 3 months old' — for the pre-arrival visa photo, and both require the photo (specifically, ONE of the two submitted) to be certified/notarized by a Justice of the Peace or Notary Public as 'a true likeness of the applicant,' using a dedicated Photo Authentication Form. Unlike the passport application instructions (which list explicit composition rules: no glasses, ears visible, chest covered, etc.), neither visa instruction sheet restates a composition specification list, a size in mm/inches, or a background color for the visa photo specifically — so none of those fields are marked verified here rather than assuming the passport's rules carry over unstated. The Grenada visa application form itself (also read) shows only a blank photo box with no printed size guide.
